title: Composition of projective-bundle morphisms over a qcqs base
statement: Let $f:A\to B$ and $g:B\to C$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Suppose $C$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. If $f$ and $g$ are projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], then $g\circ f:A\to C$ is projective in the same sense.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper] to $f:A\to B$ and $g:B\to C$: both maps are proper. Independently apply [lem-per-projective-bundle-relative-ample] to the same two maps: each is of finite type and admits a relatively ample invertible module. Thus $f$ and $g$ satisfy exactly the quasi-projectivity conditions (finite type and existence of a relatively ample invertible module); this does not require $B$ to be quasi-compact or quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 0C4P (lemma-composition-projective), first sentence; inputs Tags 01WC and 07RL.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] to the two proper maps of Step 1 to obtain properness of $g\circ f:A\to C$. Apply [lem-per-quasiprojective-qc-composition] with $X=A$, $Y=B$, $S=C$ and with the relatively ample modules supplied by Step 1. Its base hypothesis is precisely the assumed quasi-compactness of $C$. It follows that $g\circ f$ is of finite type and has a relatively ample invertible module $N$.

source.place: Tag 0C4P (lemma-composition-projective), second sentence; inputs Tags 01W3 and 0C4M.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-proper-relative-ample-projective-bundle] to $h=g\circ f$ and its module $N$. Properness and relative ampleness were proved in Step 2, and its base $C$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by assumption. The conclusion is projectivity in the projective-bundle sense, exactly as required.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0C4P (lemma-composition-projective), complete three-sentence proof, through Tags 01WC, 07RL, 01W3, 0C4M and 0BCL(1).
